node.name: Lemon Ice
node.description: Refreshingly tart and sweet, lemon ice delivers a spoonful of summer in every bite.
recipeIngredient: ¼ cup + 2 tablespoons freshly squeezed lemon juice, (from about 3 lemons)

recipeInstructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the lemon zest, lemon juice, sugar, and salt. Gradually whisk in the half & half, and continue whisking until the sugar is completely dissolved, 1 to 2 minutes.
recipeInstructions.name: In a large bowl, whisk together the lemon zest, lemon juice, sugar, and salt. Gradually whisk in the half & half, and continue whisking until the sugar is completely dissolved, 1 to 2 minutes.

recipeInstructions.text: Pour the mixture into a shallow container, such as an 8-in (20-cm) cake pan, and cover with plastic wrap. Freeze until the mixture is solid around the edges yet still mushy in the middle, about 2 hours. Stir well, cover again, and continue to freeze until completely firm, 2 to 3 hours more. Once firm, scoop into chilled bowls to serve.

review.reviewBody: I made the lemon ice recipe with oranges reducing sugar by 2 tablespoons. I tasted the orange juice before adding it to the recipe and it was borderline sweet. Next time I'd reduce by 3 tablespoons. My husband loved the recipe as I made it but I thought it a bit too sweet. I think it also depends on how sweet the oj is. I will definitely make it again. Delicious and refreshing!
This-like all of your recipes Jenn- is amazing!

Greetings Jenn. I am not one to tell a recipe developer when I modified a recipe but this is too good not to share with you. I made the lemon ice as directed. Then I followed the same recipe with lime. Most recently I followed the same recipe using tart-ish Mandarins AND one scant teaspoon of Fiori di Sicilia. Oh. My. Goodness. Creamsicle heaven. I am sure there is a future dinner here with all three citrus flavors served in desert bowls. Thank you so, so much.

Have made this twice in The past two weeks and will likely continue to make it on repeat throughout the spring/summer…it is SO good and so easy to make! Everyone who’s tried it has raved about it. Thanks so much Jen for another winner recipe! When I make it, I lightly pack the lemon zest into the teaspoon and I also cut the sugar down to 3/4c. I prefer to pour it into a silicone muffin pan before freezing…makes perfect individual portions and pops right out of the silicone pan really easily. Works great when entertaining!
So easy to make. Adored by so many! I’ve made it with lemons and Meyer lemons.
I used a stick blender to mix it and my ice cream machine.  It got fantastic. And I used heavy cream and milk. I want to try oranges instead of lemon. As a child I loved an orange cream icicle.

Oh my goodness. Half and half left over after weekend guests and  lemons fading fast resulted in a cold and creamy treat. It is so easy I feel like it is almost cheating.  I should have had to work harder to achieve something so delicious.  Thanks, Jenn.

Has anyone doubled this in a 9x13 for a larger crowd?  Didn't want to risk so I kept in 2 
8" squares.

It is so delicious and will be on repeat around here as I have 3 lemon trees.
Delicious! And easy. We made it with lime instead.
Wow!!! Just wow!!! 🤩 Perfect dessert when it is 100 degrees out!!!! So easy, so light, so cool and SO yummy!!! Thanks for all your recipes! You make me a good cook!
